claims.text: The initial Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy was produced by arc melting with multiple remelts.
The intervention changes the composition from Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 to Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15.
The composition modification will shift solidification from a complex sequence to a predominantly eutectic-dominated process under rapid cooling.
The composition modification will improve amorphous retention relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The composition modification will enhance thermal stability during reheating relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Melt spinning on a copper wheel at 40 m/s will produce approximately 20 micrometer ribbons.
The proposed structural mediator is a eutectic-dominated structure containing fine, rod-like eutectic colonies.
The eutectic-dominated structure can be retained completely in an amorphous state under rapid cooling.
Lowering phosphorus content limits formation of high-temperature phosphides.
Lowering phosphorus content decreases primary solid-solution crystallization.
Increasing Fe and Co promotes cooperative eutectic growth.
Rapid quenching suppresses elemental segregation.
Rapid quenching suppresses crystallite nucleation.
Suppression of segregation and crystallite nucleation stabilizes the amorphous phase during solidification and subsequent thermal analysis.
Rapidly melt-spun Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 ribbons will be fully amorphous.
The modified ribbons will exhibit a broad and thermally stable crystallization interval during DSC reheating at 20 K/min.
Slower-cooled, arc-melted samples of the modified alloy will undergo multiphase crystallization.
The slower-cooled modified alloy will have a simpler, more eutectic-dominated transformation than the original alloy.
The original Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy displayed limited amorphous retention and a complex sequence with multiple crystallization events.
Enhanced amorphous retention and thermal stability are expected only for thin, rapidly cooled ribbons and not for bulk or slower-cooled samples.

contradictions.description: The mediator is described as fine, rod-like eutectic colonies and the mechanism invokes cooperative eutectic growth, while the predicted rapidly cooled product is fully amorphous and nucleation is said to be suppressed. Crystalline eutectic colonies cannot simultaneously constitute a completely amorphous structure without further clarification that the eutectic description refers only to liquid composition or transformation tendency.
